content.intended_use: Certify the pointwise validity of a geodesic subgradient cut.

proofs.full_local_argument: This is a local reconstruction, not a transcription of the printed Proof. Fix all objects and variables as in the statement. The Hadamard property makes w=Log_x(y) uniquely defined. If y∈S outside H_x(v), Definition 6 gives <w,v>_x≥0. Applying the assumed subgradient inequality at z=y therefore yields f(y)≥f(x)+<v,w>_x≥f(x). Consequently f(y)<f(x) forces y∈H_x(v). If a minimizer y* exists and x is not a minimizer, then f(y*)<f(x), so every such y* lies in H_x(v)∩S. For v=0 the support inequality gives f(z)≥f(x) for every z∈S, proving that x is a minimizer. This exhausts the stated cases without assuming that an infimum is attained. The printed f(c) is not used.

assumptions: M is simply connected and has a complete Riemannian metric with sectional curvature at most zero.
x∈S and v is a subgradient of f on S at x in the stated global support-inequality sense.
statement.conclusion: For every y∈S outside H_x(v), f(y)≥f(x); hence {y∈S:f(y)<f(x)}⊆H_x(v)∩S. If a minimum is attained and x is not a minimizer, every minimizer lies in H_x(v)∩S. If v=0, x is a global minimizer on S. No attainment is asserted when the infimum is not achieved.
statement.objects_and_definitions: M is an n-dimensional Hadamard manifold, S⊆M is nonempty and geodesically convex, and f:S→R is geodesically convex. Log_x=exp_x^{-1}. Define H_x(v)={exp_x(w):<w,v>_x<0}. A supplied subgradient v∈T_xM means f(z)≥f(x)+<v,Log_x(z)>_x for every z∈S.
statement.parameter_domains: Integer n≥1; v may be zero. No probability measure, Lipschitz constant or curvature lower bound is required.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such M,S,f, every x∈S, every supplied subgradient v, and every y∈S outside H_x(v), the conclusion holds deterministically.
